pages.hook: Calling a pizza place can feel scary at first. The call is short and always follows the same steps: size, kind, extras, your name and the wait time.

mythfact.s: In the USA, “takeout” means food you take away from the restaurant.
On the phone, the restaurant asks for your name for the order.
mythfact.why: They write it on the box or bag so you can find your order.

mythfact.s: You can ask for half cheese, half pepperoni on one pizza.
mythfact.why: Half and half pizzas are common in many pizza places.

mythfact.s: Newark is the capital of New Jersey.
mythfact.why: Newark is the biggest city, but the capital is Trenton.

mythfact.s: “Mystic Pizza” is a 1988 film with Julia Roberts.
mythfact.why: It is a film about three friends who work at a pizza restaurant.

pages.title: Reading quest — Pizza for three
text: Friday night in **Newark**. Abe and his two friends are hungry. They want pizza, and nobody wants to cook. Abe picks up the phone.

“Joe’s Pizza. **How can I help you?**” a woman says. Abe answers, “**Hi. I’d like a large pizza for takeout.**” “**What kind of pizza?**” “**Half cheese, half pepperoni.**” One friend likes mushrooms, but Abe says, “Not today!”

“**Anything else?**” she asks. “**A bottle of soda, please.**” She answers, “**It’ll be twenty minutes.**” “**Great. My name is Sam**,” Abe says. “Your order will be ready soon,” she says. Abe says thank you and ends the call.
Twenty minutes later, they walk to the shop. The smell is wonderful. The box is warm in Abe’s hands. “**Pizza’s here!**” he says. They laugh and sit in the park to eat.

Abe remembers the film Mystic Pizza. In it, three young women work at a small pizza place. The place is the heart of their town. “**This hits the spot**,” says one friend. Abe smiles. A simple phone call, and a perfect Friday.
